findings.title: Irreversible hard DELETE without audit or soft-delete safeguard
findings.description: deleteCompanyByIdAndState permanently removes rows from COMPANY. Deleted rows are unrecoverable through the mapper because the statement writes no audit record, tombstone, or soft-delete column. The intended business semantics (hard vs soft delete) are unverified; this is a confirmed static observation with no runtime evidence.
findings.recommendation: Confirm that an irreversible hard delete is the intended behavior. If retention or compliance is required, replace the DELETE with a soft-delete UPDATE (state/valid-to column) or log the affected identifiers inside the enclosing transaction before deleting.

findings.title: Predicate assumes ID uniquely identifies a single target row
findings.description: The WHERE clause filters only on ID and COMPANY_STATE. If COMPANY.ID is not unique, a single call can delete multiple rows. ID uniqueness and the delete selectivity of COMPANY_STATE could not be verified against the database because this statement is static-review-only.
findings.recommendation: Verify COMPANY.ID is a unique or primary-key column. If multi-row deletes are possible, add safeguards such as a pre-delete row-count check in the transaction or DELETE ... LIMIT where supported.
